input.topic: Two friends at a railway station discover their tickets are for different destinations.
input.recentProse:
Ana y Luis están en la estación. Ana tiene una bolsa. Luis tiene una mochila. Los dos amigos quieren viajar a Madrid.

—Yo tengo mi billete —dice Ana.

—Yo también tengo mi billete —dice Luis.

Ana mira su billete.

—Mi tren sale a las diez. ¿Y tu tren?

Luis revisa su billete. Luis mira la hora.

—Mi tren también sale a las diez.

Ana mira el billete de Luis. Ana ve un nombre: Toledo.

—Luis, ¿tu destino es Toledo?

—No, mi destino es Madrid.

—Pero tu billete dice «Toledo».

Luis mira su billete otra vez.

—Sí, es verdad. Mi billete es para Toledo. ¿Tu billete es para Madrid?

Ana muestra su billete.

—Sí. Mira: Madrid.

Los dos amigos miran los billetes.

—Tenemos dos billetes para dos destinos diferentes —dice Luis.

—Sí —dice Ana—. No podemos viajar juntos con estos billetes.

Luis ve una ventanilla. Una mujer está detrás de la ventanilla.

—Podemos preguntar allí —dice Luis.

Ana toma su bolsa. Los dos amigos caminan hacia la ventanilla.

glossary.meaning: And; joins people or things.
To arrive; llegan is the present-tense form for Ana and Luis together.
To; introduces a destination or the person receiving something.
Ticket or service window at the station.
The; la is feminine singular, el masculine singular, and los masculine plural.
To put or place; pone means Luis puts his ticket down.
His, her, or your in polite speech; identifies whose ticket or destination is meant.
Travel ticket; billetes is plural.
In front of; describes where Luis places his ticket.
Woman; here, the woman working at the ticket window.
Good morning; a greeting.
My; used before a noun such as ticket.
To be; es identifies the ticket's destination.
For; indicates the destination a ticket is valid for.
But; introduces a contrast.
To want; quiero means I want and is followed here by ir.
To go; ir a introduces the place someone wants to go to.
With; describes company or what a sign contains.
To show; muestra means Ana shows her ticket.
To be able to or can; podemos means we can, followed by an infinitive such as cambiar or viajar.
To change or exchange; here, to exchange Luis's ticket.
Of or belonging to; links a ticket to its owner, a train to its departure time, or names to cities.
To look at; mira is the present-tense form used for one person.
Two.
Yes; the accent distinguishes it from si, meaning if.
A or one; used before a masculine singular noun.
One moment; a short request to wait.
Please; makes a request polite.
Screen; here, the screen the woman checks.
To wait; espera means Luis waits.
Next to; describes Luis standing beside Ana.
Hay means there is or there are; used to ask about and confirm an available place.
Place or seat available on the train.
Me; the pronoun used after para. Unlike mi meaning my, it has an accent.
To ask a question; pregunta means Luis asks.
On; here, on the train.
Train.
At ten o'clock; a las introduces a clock time.
To smile; sonríe means Luis smiles.
Very good or great; expresses satisfaction here.
To take; toma means the woman takes the old ticket.
Then or afterward; introduces the next action.
To hand over or give; entrega means the woman gives Luis a ticket.
New; describes the replacement ticket. The masculine singular ending agrees with billete.
Here you are; a polite expression when handing something to someone.
Destination; the place someone is traveling to.
To read; lee means Luis reads the ticket.
Also or too; Ana checks her ticket as well.
Now; refers to the situation after the ticket is changed.
To travel; the infinitive follows podemos, meaning we can travel.
Together; the masculine plural form refers to both friends.
Thank you.
To say; dice introduces what someone says.
Friend; amigos is the plural form referring to Ana and Luis.
To leave; salen de means the two friends leave the ticket window.
To see or notice; ve means Ana sees a sign.
Sign or information board; here, one showing numbers and city names.
Number; números is plural.
Name; nombres refers to the names of cities.
City; ciudades is plural.
To have to; tenemos que means we have to, followed here by buscar.
To look for or find; here, to locate their train.
Our; the masculine singular form agrees with tren.
She or her; con ella means with her, referring to Ana.
